classification.assetImpact: No theft and no permanent loss. Pool-wide DENIAL OF SERVICE on principal: a reverting IPhlimboHook unwinds the entire outer call, including withdraw's principal safeTransfer at :774, so EVERY staker's principal is frozen simultaneously for as long as the hook reverts. Principal remains fully recoverable — one setHook(address(0)) tx unfreezes the pool. Because PhlimboV3 has no hook-exempt exit (verified: zero pauseWithdraw, zero emergencyWithdraw), the staker has ZERO self-recovery and cannot compel the remedy.
attackPath: 1. Owner calls setHook(analyticsHook) — a legitimate, first-class, story-020-built feature. The hook is an observer: points, boosters, indexing. Owner's post-setHook smoke test PASSES; stake/withdraw/claim all work.
2. Time passes. NO owner action occurs at or near the freeze.

3. The hook begins reverting for a third-party reason it does not control — a dependency registry pauses (PoC captures RegistryPaused() = 0x24522f34 propagating unwrapped), an upgraded downstream contract changes behaviour, an oracle reverts, an arithmetic edge trips (PoC captures Panic(0x11)), or gas growth exceeds the stipend.

4. Every stake/withdraw/claim now reverts pool-wide. withdraw() still REACHES its principal safeTransfer at :774 — the transfer executes and is then unwound by the hook revert at :781. Principal is frozen.

5. No user recourse: PhlimboV3 has no hook-exempt exit. claimUnclaimable* are hook-exempt but carry only banked REWARDS, never principal. batchClaim is promo-only and phase-gated. Empirically enumerated by the PoC — no escape path exists.
6. Freeze persists until the owner notices and calls setHook(address(0)). Duration is bounded only by the owner's monitoring latency, not by any protocol mechanism.
classification.likelihood: medium-low, and NOT owner-gated at the moment of failure. Requires the optional hook to be enabled (see conditionality) — but given a hook IS enabled, the freeze needs no owner action, no attacker, and no user error. It is triggered by ordinary third-party breakage of a live external dependency, which is a routine occurrence over a protocol's lifetime. The trigger is TIME-SHIFTED away from the owner's decision, which is precisely why it evades the owner's validation.
classification.assumptions: Owner is non-malicious (Law 3). Owner has enabled the optional hook via setHook — the single load-bearing assumption, stated plainly and NOT pre-discounted. The hook is itself benign; a malicious hook is Law-3-exempt and is expressly NOT what is reported here.
classification.externalRequirements: A third-party revert inside the hook's own execution — external to PhlimboV3, external to the owner, and outside both parties' control at the moment it fires. This is a textbook C4 Medium 'external requirement'.

classifiedFindings.severityRationale: MEDIUM — confirmed, and this is the one classification in the run where the conservative default does NOT apply, because two independent lines of evidence converge on Medium. (1) LITERAL C4 FIT: Medium is 'assets not at direct risk, but the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted.' disclosureWeighing.question: The task correctly flags that IPhlimboHook.sol documents the propagation ('The owner of PhlimboV2 is trusted to set non-malicious hooks; a reverting hook will revert the outer call'), and asks whether that disclosure narrows the non-obviousness argument enough to force a downgrade. Weighed honestly, at length, and it does NOT — for four reasons, in ascending order of force.
disclosureWeighing.concession: FIRST, THE CONCESSION, stated without hedging: the disclosure is real, it is accurate, and it names this finding's exact mechanism in plain words. This is NOT an undocumented behaviour, and any framing that called the propagation itself a hidden trap would be dishonest and is rejected. A competent owner who reads this interface knows a reverting hook reverts the outer call. That genuinely narrows the footgun argument and is the strongest single point against this finding.
why_it_still_does_not_downgrade: 1. THE DISCLOSURE ADDRESSES THE CASE WE DO NOT REPORT, AND IS SILENT ON THE CASE WE DO. Read the sentence as written: 'The owner of PhlimboV2 is trusted to set NON-MALICIOUS hooks; a reverting hook will revert the outer call.' The semicolon binds the propagation to the malice frame — its plain reading is 'do not attach a hostile hook, because a hostile hook can revert your calls.' The MALICIOUS-hook case is Law-3 trusted and expressly out of scope; we do not report it. The case we DO report — a benign, correctly-written hook that begins reverting 30 days later for a third-party reason — is not addressed by that sentence at all. The disclosure and the finding barely overlap on the operative scenario.

2. THE DISCLOSED FACT AND THE UNDISCLOSED CONSEQUENCE ARE NOT THE SAME PROPOSITION. 'A reverting hook will revert the outer call' is a mechanism. 'A reverting hook permanently freezes every staker's principal with no user recourse and no escape hatch' is a consequence. On PhlimboV2 — the ONLY contract the docblock names — the mechanism was TRUE and the consequence was FALSE, because pauseWithdraw was hook-exempt (PhlimboV2.sol:280's NatSpec confirms the hook-exempt exit was DELIBERATE: 'Emergency exit mechanism... Does NOT invoke any hook'). The docblock is a V2 artifact written for a contract where its implication was survivable. story-030 deleted pauseWithdraw from V3 and did not touch the docblock. The sentence's truth value never changed; its MEANING silently became far worse. An owner is entitled to read a documented behaviour in the safety context the document was written for.

3. THE DISCLOSURE IS V2-SCOPED BY ITS OWN TEXT AND ABSENT AT THE POINT OF ACTION. Verified this run: IPhlimboHook.sol names PhlimboV2 three times and NEVER mentions V3. PhlimboV3.sol contains no hook-revert disclosure anywhere; setHook's entire NatSpec is '@notice Sets the hook contract invoked after stake/withdraw/claim. @dev Accepts address(0) to disable the hook.' The owner performing the one load-bearing action in this finding — calling setHook on V3 — is warned of nothing, and the warning that does exist elsewhere is about a different contract with a different safety profile.

4. THE PROTOCOL'S OWN CONDUCT CONTRADICTS THE DISCLOSURE'S IMPLICATION, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE SURPRISE GENUINE. Three consecutive stories (027 stable/promo bank, 029 non-reverting reward forwarding, 031 phUSD mint bank) were spent for the express purpose of ensuring a failing reward leg can never freeze principal. The contract-profile asserts INV-01 ('A user's principal is never frozen by a failing reward payout') HOLDS at f279c62. An owner who watched those three stories land, and who reads that invariant, will reasonably believe 'principal cannot freeze on a reward-path failure' is now a property of this system. In the hooked configuration it is not. When a protocol spends three stories buying an invariant and then asserts it holds, a residual leg that defeats it is a surprise regardless of what a V2-era interface docblock says. Law 3's test — 'would a competent, non-malicious owner be SURPRISED by this consequence?' — resolves YES on the consequence even though it resolves NO on the mechanism. The finding is about the consequence.
disclosureWeighing.netEffect: The disclosure moves this finding from 'undocumented trap' to 'documented mechanism whose safety context was silently deleted and whose governing doc was never updated.' That is still a Medium availability hazard; it is not a Low. What the disclosure DOES earn is the F-11-02 spec-conformance leg (the doc is stale and misplaced) and a softening of the report's tone: this must be written up as an inherited-mechanism/lost-mitigation finding, NOT as 'the protocol hid a trap.' The loss is one migrating user's ACCRUED phUSD REWARD entitlement for a single position: PhlimboV3 credits it to unclaimablePhUSDOf[MigratorV2V3], an address with no pull, while the user's phUSDDebt is realigned by the caller (:715) so their on-chain entitlement is discharged. Unrecoverable ON-CHAIN by any party (verified: emergencyTransfer and withdrawAll both sweep balanceOf, and there is no backing balance to sweep). Recoverable OUT-OF-BAND at ~zero cost: setMinter(owner,true) then mint(user,amount) — verified available and reversible this run.

PRECONDITION 2: phUSD mint-authority outage for PhlimboV3 — e.g. an INDIVIDUAL setMinter(phlimbo,false), typically to contain an unrelated minter incident on the shared ecosystem token. Must be individual, not global: a global revokeAllMintPrivileges would also break PhlimboV2's bare inline mint (PhlimboV2.sol:495), reverting migrateOne, which migrate catches as UserMigrationSkipped — leaving the user untouched and UNHARMED.

PRECONDITION 3: a migrator second/straggler pass over a user who ALREADY holds a V3 position. Verified: _claimRewards early-returns at :898-900 on `userDetails.amount == 0`, so a first-pass migrant never reaches the bank.
1. Migrator calls stake(user, amount); _claimRewards(user, beneficiary=migrator) accrues pendingPhUSDAmount > 0.

2. phUSD.mint(migrator, amount) reverts (authority revoked). The try/catch at :913-918 swallows it and banks to unclaimablePhUSDOf[migrator]; PhUSDMintFailed is emitted (without a reason — see CLASS-11-006).

4. The user's V3 position is created and their V2 position consumed; the migration reports success. The reward accrual is stranded at an address with no pull, permanently, on-chain.
5. Owner's remedy (out-of-band, ~zero cost): re-grant authority, then setMinter(owner,true) + phUSD.mint(user, amount) to make the user whole. FlaxToken has no supply cap.

classifiedFindings.severityRationale: LOW — but reached independently, not by ratifying the majority. C4 Medium offers exactly two doors and this finding fails one and squeaks under the other. Door 1, 'protocol function or availability impacted': NO, decisively. Principal flows freely, migration completes, nothing is bricked — which is precisely what story-031 bought. Door 2, 'leak value with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements': this is the RIGHT clause and the dissent is correct to cite it; the assumptions and external requirements are all present. It fails on MAGNITUDE and REMEDY COST, not on shape. What is lost is a single position's reward accrual — not principal — for the narrow subset of straggler-pass migrants, on a path that is dead code at the shipped config, where nothing is transferred to anyone and the protocol's balance sheet is untouched because the tokens were never minted. The 'permanent' in the dissent is true ON-CHAIN and false IN PRACTICE: the entitlement is re-issuable at zero marginal cost from an uncapped mint the owner controls. A bookkeeping error correctable by two txs, on dead code, affecting rewards and not principal, is a Low. Calling it Medium would overstate, and the pipeline rejects overstatement. The decisive comparison is with V3-L-15 (Low): the dissent argues this is STRICTLY WORSE because V3-L-15's Low rests on emergencyTransfer recoverability that provably does not reach the un-minted phUSD bank. True on-chain — but it inverts once you price the remedies. V3-L-15's remedy is emergencyTransfer, a TERMINAL ejector seat that kills the protocol to recover the value. This finding's remedy is two txs that harm nothing. On PRACTICAL recoverability — the axis that actually determines user outcome — this finding is BETTER off than the Low it claims to outrank. Both are Low.

dissentAdjudication.whyTheSeverityIsNOTAdopted: The Medium rests entirely on the word 'unrecoverable.' That word is doing work it cannot bear. It is true on-chain and false in practice, and severity tracks user outcome, not on-chain mechanism. I did not take this on the dedup's word — I stress-tested the remedy in source, because if it had failed, the Low would have collapsed and I would have carried the dissent's Medium. FlaxToken.mint (:58) is NOT owner-callable; it is minter-gated (require(minterInfo.canMint) + a mintVersion match), so 'the owner just mints them whole' is not automatically available and had to be checked. It survives: setMinter (:44) is onlyOwner and re-stamps the CURRENT mintVersion, and revokeAllMintPrivileges (:88) merely increments mintVersion rather than permanently sealing supply — so the outage is REVERSIBLE and the owner can always authorize themselves and mint. Had revokeAllMintPrivileges been an irreversible supply lock (a common and plausible design for a token kill-switch), the remedy would have evaporated, 'unrecoverable' would have become true in practice as well as on-chain, and this finding would be a Medium. It is not. The Low's foundation is verified, not assumed.

classification.assetImpact: Post-terminal double-pay. emergencyTransfer (:360-378) is a BALANCE sweep + _pause(). It neutralizes the stable and promo banks as a side effect (their tokens are gone, so their pulls revert), but CANNOT reach the phUSD bank: the tokens were never minted, so the sweep cannot see them, and claimUnclaimablePhUSD (:644) is deliberately NOT whenNotPaused, so the pause does not stop it either (verified in source: `function claimUnclaimablePhUSD() external nonReentrant` — no pause modifier). While PhlimboV3 retains mint authority, every outstanding bank entry stays pullable AFTER the ejector seat has fired, minting brand-new phUSD supply the sweep never accounted for.
attackPath: PRECONDITION 1 (NOT SHIPPED): non-zero desiredAPYBps — same DEDUP-04 dormancy gate as CLASS-11-002.
PRECONDITION 2: a non-empty residual phUSD bank at sweep time (i.e. some prior mint-authority outage banked entries that were never pulled).

1. Owner fires the terminal ejector seat: emergencyTransfer sweeps phUSD/rewardToken/promo balances to the recipient and _pause()s the contract. Owner reasonably concludes the protocol is wound down and all obligations are extinguished — the other two banks visibly died with the sweep.
2. A bank holder calls claimUnclaimablePhUSD() on the paused, drained contract. It SUCCEEDS (not whenNotPaused).
3. phUSD.mint fires: FRESH, unbacked supply is minted after the wind-down (PoC: phUSD.totalSupply() == supplyBefore + earned, on a contract with balanceOf == 0 and paused == true).
4. Loss is dilution of phUSD holders, arising from the owner's oversight in the wind-down sequence — not from any adversarial act.
classification.likelihood: low — double-gated, requires the terminal ejector seat to fire (already a rare, protocol-ending event) with a non-empty residual bank, on a reward stream that is off at the shipped config.
classification.assumptions: Owner is non-malicious. Owner fires emergencyTransfer intending to terminate all obligations. PhlimboV3 still holds phUSD mint authority at that moment.
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond the wind-down itself. The claimant needs no privilege and is acting in good faith.

classifiedFindings.severityRationale: LOW — confirmed. No availability impact, no attacker construction, no theft: the holder is claiming exactly what the contract records as owed. The harm is unbacked dilution arising from an owner oversight in the wind-down sequence, double-gated (dormant reward stream + non-empty residual bank), and fully preventable by a ONE-LINE RUNBOOK STEP. It does not reach Medium: there is no function or availability impact, and while there is a value leak, it requires a rare terminal event to have already fired and is preventable at zero cost by an operator following a documented sequence. QA would understate it — fresh unbacked supply minted after a terminal wind-down is a real economic consequence with a live PoC, and this project has a documented cross-system unbacked-phUSD theme (cf. yield-claim-nft DEDUP-001) that makes silent post-terminal minting worth a Low rather than a note.

An integrator consuming them as an entitlement oracle would double-count.

2. The hooked token's callback fires while debts are still stale (realignment happens caller-side, after _claimRewards returns).
3. The callback calls pendingPhUSD(user) on PhlimboV3 — a view, so nonReentrant does not apply.
4. The view returns FULL pending for value already minted/transferred. The integrator double-counts. PhlimboV3's own accounting remains correct throughout.

findings.title: story-031 falsified TWO documented behaviours it did not update: MigratorV2V3's delta-capture assumption, and PhlimboV3's own claimed bank-recoverability semantics

deviations.documented: 'Any V3 auto-claim (second pass only) lands here and is included in the deltas below'
deviations.actual: FALSE for the banked case. A banked accrual does NOT land in the migrator's balance, so the delta at :260 reads 0 and _forward:268 forwards nothing. story-031 defeated this assumption and did not update the comment.
deviations.verified: Confirmed in source at f279c62 by this agent.

deviations.documented: 'A pull that fails because authority is still missing SHOULD revert, leaving the bank intact (exactly the claimUnclaimableStable recoverability semantics).'
deviations.actual: The claimed recoverability semantics DO NOT HOLD when the beneficiary is a contract with no call-through. The docblock presumes the beneficiary CAN pull and reasons only about the pull FAILING; for the MigratorV2V3 beneficiary there is no pull at all, so 'leaving the bank intact' means 'leaving it permanently unreachable', not 'preserving it for a later retry'. The docblock asserts a recoverability property the bank does not universally have.
deviations.verified: Confirmed in source at f279c62 by this agent (docblock read in full; MigratorV2V3's complete external surface enumerated).

findings.whyRoutedHere: Per Law 2 and the classifier's rule 6: a deviation from documented behaviour is tagged faithfulness:true and routed to the spec-conformance channel at honest severity, NEVER dropped into QA/gas noise — even when the associated security finding is only a Low. The second deviation is the more important of the two: the dissent noted the docblock 'promises the opposite' of what happens, and that observation SURVIVES the Low severity intact. It is the clearest single artefact showing the strand was unintended rather than accepted.
findings.fixGuidance: Correct both comments as part of whichever CLASS-11-002 fix is chosen. If the pull-on-behalf variant is adopted, the :637-643 docblock becomes TRUE as written and only the MigratorV2V3 comment needs updating — which is a further point in that fix's favour.

findings.title: The only documentation governing hook-revert propagation is a V2-scoped docblock whose safety context story-030 deleted from V3, and PhlimboV3.setHook warns of nothing

deviations.documented: 'Hooks fire AFTER all internal state mutations and external token transfers complete, inside PhlimboV2's nonReentrant guard. The owner of PhlimboV2 is trusted to set non-malicious hooks; a reverting hook will revert the outer call.'
deviations.actual: The docblock names PhlimboV2 THREE times and never mentions V3, yet V3 imports and relies on this interface. On V2 the statement's implication was survivable (pauseWithdraw was hook-exempt — PhlimboV2.sol:280 NatSpec: 'Emergency exit mechanism... Does NOT invoke any hook'). On V3, story-030 deleted pauseWithdraw, so the identical sentence now means 'permanent pool-wide principal freeze with no exit'. The document's truth value is unchanged; its IMPLICATION changed radically and silently, and nothing was updated.
deviations.verified: Confirmed in source at f279c62: zero 'pauseWithdraw' and zero 'emergencyWithdraw' occurrences in PhlimboV3.sol; IPhlimboHook.sol read in full.

deviations.documented: '@notice Sets the hook contract invoked after stake/withdraw/claim. @dev Accepts address(0) to disable the hook.' — that is the docblock IN FULL.
deviations.actual: No warning whatsoever at the point of the one load-bearing action in CLASS-11-001. An owner calling setHook on V3 is told nothing about revert propagation, nothing about the absence of a hook-exempt exit, and nothing about the consequence for principal.

findings.alsoAffectsAnAssertedInvariant: The contract-profile asserts INV-01 ('A user's principal is never frozen by a failing reward payout') HOLDS at f279c62. It survives only under a narrow literal reading of 'reward payout'; the property three stories (027/029/031) were spent buying does NOT hold in the hooked configuration. This is a conformance gap between the protocol's asserted invariants and its actual guarantees, and it materially amplifies CLASS-11-001's non-obviousness.
findings.whyRoutedHere: Raised as spec-conformance rather than folded silently into CLASS-11-001's Medium because it is independently actionable: even if the try/catch fix is declined, the documentation must be corrected, and correcting it is nearly free. It is also the honest counterweight to CLASS-11-001 — the propagation IS documented somewhere, and this F-label is where that fact is recorded rather than being quietly omitted from the Medium's write-up.
findings.fixGuidance: Whether or not the try/catch lands: (1) rewrite IPhlimboHook's docblock to be contract-neutral and to state the CONSEQUENCE, not just the mechanism, and to distinguish the malicious-hook case (trusted) from the benign-hook-breaks-later case (the real hazard); (2) add the warning to PhlimboV3.setHook's own NatSpec, where the owner will actually see it; (3) reconcile INV-01's statement with the hooked configuration.

contestedClassifications.CLASS-11-001 (hook principal freeze) = M: The IPhlimboHook disclosure is real, accurate, and names the mechanism — but it addresses the MALICIOUS-hook case (Law-3 exempt, not what is reported), is V2-scoped by its own text, is absent from PhlimboV3.setHook entirely, and its benign implication on V2 depended on a pauseWithdraw escape that story-030 deleted from V3 without updating the doc. The mechanism is disclosed; the CONSEQUENCE is not. Medium is confirmed principally on INTERNAL CONSISTENCY: this project already rates the identical impact shape (all stakers frozen, no self-recovery) at Medium twice (V3-M-05, V3-M-07-via-symmetry-rule), and the hook leg fits C4's 'external requirements' clause BETTER than V3-M-07 does, since it needs no owner action at the moment of freeze. contestedClassifications.CLASS-11-002 (migrator phUSD strand) = L: The Medium dissent was adjudicated on its merits, not out-voted. Its MECHANISM is ACCEPTED and adopted into the fix guidance: story-031 genuinely converted a loud, self-healing failure into a silent, permanent one on the migrator leg — the fix introduced a new loss path, and any fix must restore LOUDNESS, not just reachability. Its SEVERITY is rejected on one axis: 'unrecoverable' is true on-chain and false in practice. I stress-tested the remedy in source rather than taking it on trust — FlaxToken.mint is minter-gated, not owner-callable, so the remedy required verification; it survives because setMinter is onlyOwner and re-stamps the current mintVersion, and revokeAllMintPrivileges only increments mintVersion (reversible, not a permanent supply lock). Had it been irreversible, this would be a Medium. Combined with rewards-not-principal, nothing minted so no balance-sheet impact, triple-gating, and gate 1 (desiredAPYBps==0) making the path dead code at the shipped config, Low is the honest label.
